name: Youth Initiation Culture — A CorpSec Threat Assessment
author: Vantablack Metro Desk — Kira Mensah-Okoye, staff correspondent
description:
CorpSec has identified at least fourteen distinct youth gang initiation rituals currently active across Tier 1 and Tier 2 districts, ranging from the performative to the genuinely dangerous to the inexplicable. What follows is a summary compiled from CorpSec surveillance reports, Shelf community worker interviews, and — in three cases — the teenagers themselves, who described their initiations with a mixture of pride and the specific bravado that conceals fear.

The most common initiation remains the Blackout Run: the recruit disables their BCI using black-market suppression software and walks a designated route through a surveilled district without being flagged by automated systems. The route is chosen by senior gang members and always passes through at least two high-security zones. Success means the recruit has proven they can move through the city invisible. Failure means CorpSec detention, which carries its own perverse status — a recruit who gets caught and doesn't talk earns respect equivalent to completing the run. The suppression software is unreliable. Three teenagers have suffered permanent BCI damage this year from botched suppression.

The Volt Kiss has emerged in the Circuit district: the recruit holds a live electrical contact from an exposed junction box while reciting the gang's founding oath from memory. The contact delivers a painful but theoretically non-lethal shock. Duration varies by gang — the Neon Vipers require eleven seconds, the Glassbreakers require the full oath which takes approximately forty. Two hospitalized this quarter. One death, unreported by the family because reporting would mean CorpSec involvement in the district. The Digit Jackals require a more technological initiation — the recruit must hack a specific CorpSec surveillance node and replace the feed with a pre-recorded loop for sixty seconds without detection. This is genuinely skilled work and the Jackals have the lowest recruitment rate and highest average competence of any youth gang in the city.

The rituals that concern CorpSec most are not the dangerous ones but the strange ones. The Gutter Prophets require recruits to spend a night in the Underworld — not the upper maintenance tunnels but deep, past the service corridors, into the unmapped sections. Recruits return changed in ways community workers describe as "quieter." They won't discuss what they saw. They don't need to — the other Gutter Prophets already know, which implies they all see the same thing. The Coffin Nails require recruits to lie in an open grave in the Old Harbor reclamation yard for the duration of one night. The grave is not dug for them — they must find one that was dug and abandoned. The fact that such graves exist regularly enough to sustain a gang's initiation cycle is itself a data point nobody at CorpSec has flagged.

The newest and most disturbing initiation belongs to a gang that calls itself the Threshold Walkers. Their ritual: the recruit must find a door that opens to somewhere it shouldn't. Not a metaphor. The recruit searches the district for spatial anomalies — doors that lead to rooms larger than the building contains, stairwells that descend further than the foundation allows, alleys that are longer on the inside than the outside. The recruit must enter, stay for one hour, and return. CorpSec considers this superstitious nonsense. Community workers in the Shelf consider it the most dangerous initiation in the city, because the doors exist, and some of the recruits who walk through them come back different, and some of them don't come back. The Threshold Walkers have a dropout rate of zero. This is not because no one quits. It is because the ones who would quit are the ones who didn't come back.
story_hooks: A Threshold Walker recruit returns from her initiation and immediately asks to speak to the gang's founder. She describes what she saw on the other side of the door: a version of the Shelf where the buildings are the same but nobody lives in them. The streets are clean. The lights are on. Every door is open. The founder listens without expression and says: "You found the quiet city. Everyone finds the quiet city. Don't go back." She goes back.

CorpSec raids a Gutter Prophet safe house and finds a wall covered in drawings — all by different hands, all depicting the same scene from the deep Underworld. The drawings show a chamber with something in it. The something is different in every drawing but occupies the same space. CorpSec classifies the drawings and seals the safe house. The drawings reappear on the sealed door within a week, drawn from the outside, in a style that matches no known member.
